(a) Retroactive Effective Date.—Except as provided in subsection (b) and section 9, this Act and the amendments made by this Act shall apply with respect to any sole survivorship discharge granted after September 11, 2001. 
    (b) Date of Enactment Effective Date for Certain Amendments.—The amendments made by sections 4, 7, and 8 shall apply with respect to any sole survivorship discharge granted after the date of the enactment of this Act. 
    (c) Sole Survivorship Discharge Defined.—In this section, the term “sole survivorship discharge” means the separation of a member from the Armed Forces, at the request of the member, pursuant to the Department of Defense policy permitting the early separation of a member who is the only surviving child in a family in which—
        (1) the father or mother or one or more siblings—
            (A) served in the Armed Forces; and 
            (B) was killed, died as a result of wounds, accident, or disease, is in a captured or missing in action status, or is permanently 100 percent disabled or hospitalized on a continuing basis (and is not employed gainfully because of the disability or hospitalization); and  
        (2) the death, status, or disability did not result from the intentional misconduct or willful neglect of the parent or 
sibling and was not incurred during a period of unauthorized absence.

fable.w: This section only sets effective dates and defines "sole survivorship discharge"; it creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, outside consultation, or right to sue. The tempting reading is that separation "at the request of the member" is outside input, but that is an individual service member's request for a personal discharge, akin to an application, not participation in a federal policy decision.
fable.s: the term “sole survivorship discharge” means the separation of a member from the Armed Forces, at the request of the member

opus.w: This section only sets effective dates and defines "sole survivorship discharge." The member's request for a discharge is an individual asking for a status or benefit, which the definition excludes as an application. It is not participation in a federal policy decision. Nothing else involves a party outside the federal government in any decision process.
opus.s: the term “sole survivorship discharge” means the separation of a member from the Armed Forces, at the request of the member, pursuant to the Department of Defense policy
opus.b: 1. **Analysis.** The tempting reading is that the phrase "at the request of the member" brings an outside party into a federal decision. It doesn't. A service member asking for their own discharge is like applying for a benefit, and the definition excludes applications. The section otherwise only sets effective dates and defines a term. It has no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or right to sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section defines the term 'sole survivorship discharge' and establishes the effective dates for the Act. It describes the criteria for eligibility (e.g., being the only surviving child of a service member who died or was disabled) but does not require the federal government to consult or coordinate with any outside parties (such as family members, states, or the public) before making a decision. The definition relies on factual conditions rather than a participatory process.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the definition of "sole survivorship discharge" involves family members (parents, siblings) whose status triggers the discharge, implying some form of interaction or consultation with them. However, the text merely defines a legal term based on objective facts (death, disability, service record) and does not require the government to consult, coordinate with, or seek input from these family members before making the decision. The process described is administrative and based on statutory criteria, not participatory.
